title.zh: 卷三百二十二 列傳第八十一 何郯 吳中復 陳薦 王獵 孫思恭 周孟陽 齊恢 楊繪 劉庠 朱京
title.en: Volume 322 Biographies 81: He Tan, Wu Zhongfu, Chen Jian, Wang Lie, Sun Sigong, Zhou Mengyang, Qi Hui, Yang Hui, Liu Xiang, Zhu Jing
title.raw: 卷三百二十二 列傳第八十一 何郯 吳中復 陳薦 王獵 孫思恭 周孟陽 齊恢 楊繪 劉庠 朱京 Volume 322 Biographies 81: He Tan, Wu Zhongfu, Chen Jian, Wang Lie, Sun Sigong, Zhou Mengyang, Qi Hui, Yang Hui, Liu Xiang, Zhu Jing

sentences.zh: 何郯，字聖從，本陵州人，徙成都。

translations.literal: He Tan, styled Shengcong, was originally a native of Ling Prefecture and moved to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He Tan, whose courtesy name was Shengcong, came from Ling Prefecture but later settled in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 第進士，由太常博士為監察御史，轉殿中侍御史，言事無所避。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; from Erudite of the Grand Music Office he became Supervising Censor, then transferred to Palace Censor-in-Attendance, remonstrating without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree, he rose from Erudite of the Grand Music Office to Supervising Censor and then Palace Censor-in-Attendance, speaking out on public affairs without flinching.

sentences.zh: 王拱辰罷三司使守亳，已而留經筵，郯乞正其營求之罪。

translations.literal: Wang Gongchen was removed as Commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments and sent to guard Bo; soon after he was kept at the imperial lecture hall, and Tan requested that his crime of scheming for gain be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gongchen lost the commissionership of the Three Fiscal Departments and was posted to Bo, only to be retained at the imperial lecture hall, Tan demanded that his corrupt self-seeking be formally punished.

sentences.zh: 石介死，樞密使夏竦讒其詐，朝廷下京東體實，郯與張昪極陳竦奸狀，事得寢。

translations.literal: When Shi Jie died, Privy Councilor Xia Song slandered him as feigning death; the court sent investigators to the capital east circuit to verify the facts. Tan and Zhang Bian fully exposed Song's treachery, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Jie's death, Privy Councilor Xia Song accused him of faking his demise, and the court dispatched investigators to the eastern capital circuit. Tan and Zhang Bian laid bare Song's villainy in detail, and the inquiry was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 楊懷敏以衛卒之亂，猶為副都知，郯又與昪及魚周詢論之。

translations.literal: Because of the guard mutiny, Yang Huaimin still held the post of Vice Director-in-Chief; Tan again discussed the matter with Bian and Yu Zhouxun.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaimin remained Vice Director-in-Chief despite the palace guard mutiny, and Tan once more joined Bian and Yu Zhouxun in protesting the appointment.

sentences.zh: 仁宗召諭云：「懷敏實先覺變，宜有所寬假。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong summoned and instructed them, saying: "Huaimin truly detected the disturbance first and ought to receive some leniency."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong called them in and said, "Huaimin was the first to sense the mutiny; he deserves some measure of clemency."

sentences.zh: 郯等皆言不可，卒出之。

translations.literal: Tan and the others all said it could not be done, and in the end Huaimin was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan and his colleagues all objected, and Yang Huaimin was dismissed in the end.

sentences.zh: 郯爭辨尤力。

translations.literal: Tan argued most forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Tan pressed his case with exceptional vigor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古有碎首諫者，卿能之乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In antiquity there were those who dashed their heads remonstrating; can you do that?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "In old times men would shatter their skulls rather than hold their tongues—would you do as much?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「古者君不從諫，則臣有碎首；

translations.literal: He replied: "In antiquity, when the ruler did not heed remonstrance, ministers had to dash their heads;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "In antiquity, ministers broke their heads only when rulers refused counsel;

sentences.zh: 今陛下受諫如流，臣何敢掠美而歸過君父。」

translations.literal: now Your Majesty receives remonstrance like flowing water—how dare I steal credit and shift blame onto my sovereign and father?"
translations.idiomatic: but Your Majesty welcomes remonstrance as freely as running water. How could I claim merit for myself and lay fault at the feet of my sovereign and father?"

sentences.zh: 帝欣納之。

translations.literal: The emperor gladly accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the reply with evident pleasure.

sentences.zh: 夏竦倡張貴妃之功，諫官王贄遂言賊根本起於皇后閣，請究其事，冀搖動中宮，而陰為妃地。

translations.literal: Xia Song promoted the merits of Consort Zhang; remonstrance official Wang Zan then said the root of the banditry lay in the empress's quarters and asked that the matter be investigated, hoping to shake the inner palace while secretly clearing ground for the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song trumpeted Consort Zhang's achievements, and remonstrance official Wang Zan claimed the rebellion had its origin in the empress's apartments, urging an investigation in the hope of unsettling the inner court while quietly advancing the consort's cause.

sentences.zh: 帝以語郯，郯曰：「此奸人之謀也。」

translations.literal: The emperor told this to Tan, and Tan said: "This is the plot of wicked men."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor repeated this to Tan, Tan replied, "This is a villain's scheme."

sentences.zh: 乃止不究。

translations.literal: The investigation was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: The inquiry was stopped.

sentences.zh: 竦負罪不去，郯等奏出知河南，竦乞留京師。

translations.literal: Song, though guilty, would not leave office; Tan and others memorialized that he be sent out to serve as prefect of Henan, but Song begged to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Though guilty, Xia Song refused to leave court; Tan and his colleagues memorialized for his appointment as prefect of Henan, while Song pleaded to stay in the capital.

sentences.zh: 郯言：「佞人在君側，為善政累，願勿革前命。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "A flatterer at the ruler's side is a burden on good government; I beg that the earlier order not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Tan argued, "With a sycophant at the sovereign's elbow, sound governance suffers. Do not revoke the earlier decree."

sentences.zh: 竦遂行。

translations.literal: Song then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song left the capital.

sentences.zh: 時詔群臣陳左右朋邪、中外險詐，久而無所行。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered ministers to report factional flatterers at court and deceit inside and out, but for a long time nothing was done.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had called on officials to expose court factions and deceit at home and abroad, yet for a long time no action followed.

sentences.zh: 郯請閱實其是否，因言曰：「誠以待物，物必應以誠。

translations.literal: Tan requested that the truth of the reports be examined, and further said: "Sincerity in treating things—things will respond with sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Tan asked that each accusation be verified, adding, "Treat the world with sincerity, and the world will answer in kind.

sentences.zh: 誠與疑，治亂之本也，不可以一臣詐而疑眾臣，一士詐而疑眾士。

translations.literal: Sincerity and suspicion are the root of order and disorder; one cannot suspect all ministers because one minister is deceitful, nor all scholars because one scholar is deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: Trust and doubt are the foundations of peace and chaos. One deceitful minister must not make you doubt every minister; one deceitful scholar must not poison your faith in every scholar.

sentences.zh: 且擇官者宰相之職，今用一吏，則疑其從私，故細務或勞於親決。

translations.literal: Moreover, selecting officials is the chancellor's duty; now if one clerk is used, it is suspected he was chosen from private favor, so minor affairs may exhaust the ruler in personal decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing officials belongs to the chancellor, yet if a single clerk is appointed, you suspect favoritism—so petty business drags the throne into endless personal adjudication.

sentences.zh: 分閫者將帥之任，今專一事，則疑其異圖，故多端而加羈制。

translations.literal: Holding a frontier command is the general's charge; now if he handles one matter alone, it is suspected he has another design, so many restrictions are added.
translations.idiomatic: Command of a frontier sector is a general's trust, yet let him act on one matter and you suspect treason—so he is hedged about with endless restraints.

sentences.zh: 博訪者大臣之體，今見一士，則疑其請託。

translations.literal: Broad consultation is the great minister's manner; now if one scholar is seen, it is suspected he came through solicitation.
translations.idiomatic: Broad consultation befits a great minister, yet the sight of one scholar makes you suspect backdoor pleading.

sentences.zh: 相先後者士之常，今進其類，則疑為朋黨。

translations.literal: Putting one another forward is ordinary among scholars; now if their kind is promoted, it is suspected to be a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars naturally recommend their peers; promote several of the same stamp and you cry "faction."

sentences.zh: 君臣交疑，而欲天下無否塞之患，不可得矣。」

translations.literal: If ruler and ministers mutually suspect one another, then to wish that the realm have no obstruction and blockage—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When sovereign and ministers eye one another with suspicion, you cannot expect the realm to remain free of obstruction and deadlock."

sentences.zh: 都知王守忠以修祭器勞，遷景福殿使，給兩使留後奉。

translations.literal: Director-in-Chief Wang Shouzhong, for labor on ritual vessels, was promoted to Commissioner of the Hall of Glorious Blessings and granted the salary of a commissioner-in-residence of two circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouzhong, Director-in-Chief, was rewarded for overseeing ritual vessels with promotion to Commissioner of the Hall of Glorious Blessings and the emoluments of a dual-circuit commissioner-in-residence.

sentences.zh: 郯曰：「守忠勞薄賞重。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Shouzhong's service was slight and the reward heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Tan protested, "Shouzhong's service was modest, the reward extravagant.

sentences.zh: 舊制，內臣遙領止於廉察。

translations.literal: By old regulation, eunuchs holding remote posts stopped at surveillance commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Under longstanding practice, eunuchs on nominal provincial posts were limited to surveillance commissions.

sentences.zh: 今雖不授留後，而先給其祿；

translations.literal: Now though the post of commissioner-in-residence is not granted, the salary is given first;
translations.idiomatic: Now, though no commissioner-in-residence title is granted, the salary comes first;

sentences.zh: 既得其祿，必得其官；

translations.literal: once the salary is obtained, the office must follow;
translations.idiomatic: once the pay is in hand, the office inevitably follows;

sentences.zh: 若又從之，則何求不可。」

translations.literal: if this too is granted, then what request could fail?"
translations.idiomatic: grant that as well, and no demand will be refused."

sentences.zh: 既又詔許如正班。

translations.literal: Later another edict permitted him to sit in the regular court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Soon another edict allowed him to take his seat among regular court ranks.

sentences.zh: 守忠移閤門，欲綴本品坐宴，郯又言：「祖宗之制，未有內臣坐殿上者。

translations.literal: Shouzhong went to the Gate of Transmission and wished to take his original rank to sit at the banquet; Tan again said: "The institutions of the ancestors never had eunuchs seated in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong appeared at the Gate of Transmission intending to banquet in hall by his former rank. Tan objected again: "Never under the founders' institutions did a eunuch sit upon the palace dais.

sentences.zh: 此弊一開，所損不細。」

translations.literal: Once this abuse is opened, the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: Let this breach open, and the damage will be far from small."

sentences.zh: 守忠聞之，不敢赴。

translations.literal: On hearing this, Shouzhong did not dare attend.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Shouzhong dared not attend.

sentences.zh: 知雜御史闕，執政欲進其黨，帝以郯不阿權勢，越次用之。

translations.literal: The post of Supervising Censor with Miscellaneous Duties was vacant; the chief ministers wished to advance their faction, but the emperor, because Tan did not fawn on power, used him out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Supervising Censor with Miscellaneous Duties post fell vacant, the chief ministers wanted their own man, but the emperor skipped the queue for Tan, who refused to truckle to power.

sentences.zh: 郯遍歷三院，有直聲。

translations.literal: Tan passed through all three censorial bureaus and had a reputation for upright speech.
translations.idiomatic: He served in all three censorial bureaus and earned a name for fearless speech.

sentences.zh: 晚節頗回畏，因地震言陰盛臣強，以譏切韓琦；

translations.literal: In his later years he turned somewhat timid; because of an earthquake he spoke of yin flourishing and ministers strong, thereby cutting at Han Qi;
translations.idiomatic: In later life he grew cautious. After an earthquake he spoke of yin overpowering yang and ministers growing too strong—a veiled attack on Han Qi;

sentences.zh: 又乞召還王陶以迎合上意，由是聲名損於御史時也。

translations.literal: he also begged to recall Wang Tao to suit the emperor's mind, and thereby his reputation fell from what it had been as censor.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked that Wang Tao be recalled to please the throne, and his standing never again matched his censorial days.

sentences.zh: 以母老求西歸，加直龍圖閣、知漢州。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested to return west, and was given Directorship of the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointment as prefect of Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother aged, he sought to return west and was made Directorship of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 將行，上疏言：「張堯佐緣後宮親，叨竊非據，外庭竊議，謂將處以二府。

translations.literal: About to depart, he submitted a memorial saying: "Zhang Yaozuo, by kinship with the inner palace, usurps an unfitting post; outside court they whisper that he will be placed in the two departments.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, he memorialized: "Zhang Yaozuo holds office he does not deserve through inner-palace kinship, and rumor outside court says he is bound for the two chief ministries.

sentences.zh: 若此命一出，言事之臣，必以死爭之。

translations.literal: If this appointment is issued, remonstrating ministers will surely contend to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Issue that appointment, and remonstrators will fight to the death against it.

sentences.zh: 倘罷堯佐則傷恩，黜言者則累德，累德、傷恩，皆為不可。

translations.literal: If Yaozuo is dismissed, kindness is wounded; if the speakers are removed, virtue is burdened—both burdening virtue and wounding kindness are impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss Yaozuo and you wound imperial grace; silence the critics and you stain virtue—neither can be borne.

sentences.zh: 臣謂莫若富貴堯佐而不假之以權，如李用和可也。」

translations.literal: Your servant thinks it best to enrich Yaozuo but not lend him power, as with Li Yonghe."
translations.idiomatic: Better to enrich Yaozuo without giving him power, as was done for Li Yonghe."

sentences.zh: 其後卒罷堯佐宣徽之命。

translations.literal: Afterward the order making Yaozuo Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service was indeed withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the appointment of Yaozuo as Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 進集賢殿修撰、知梓州，擢天章閣待制，還判銀臺司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature and made prefect of Zi Prefecture, then elevated to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and returned to judge the Silver Terrace Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature and prefect of Zi Prefecture, then to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall, returning to judge the Silver Terrace Office.

sentences.zh: 時封駁之職廢，郯乞準故事，凡詔敕並由門下，從之。

translations.literal: At the time the duty of sealing and returning edicts had lapsed; Tan requested that by precedent all edicts pass through the Gate Office, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of sealing and returning improper edicts had fallen into disuse; Tan restored the old rule that all edicts pass through the Gate Office, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 唐介出荊南，敕過門下，郯封還之，介復留諫院。

translations.literal: Tang Jie was sent out to Jingnan; the edict passed the Gate Office and Tan sealed and returned it, and Jie remained in the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Jie was ordered to Jingnan, Tan sealed and returned the edict at the Gate Office, and Jie stayed at the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士，為河東都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made Transport Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Transport Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 故相梁適帥太原，病不能事，內臣蘇安靜鈐轄兵馬，怙寵不法，皆劾奏之。

translations.literal: The former chancellor Liang Shi commanded at Taiyuan but was ill and unable to administer; the eunuch Su Anjing controlled the troops, relying on favor and breaking the law—all were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Former chancellor Liang Shi held Taiyuan but was too ill to govern; eunuch Su Anjing controlled the army, arrogant and lawless—Tan impeached them all.

sentences.zh: 歷知永興、河南。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Yongxing and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Yongxing and Henan in turn.

sentences.zh: 治平末，再知梓州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhiping era he again became prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Zhiping era he was again appointed prefect of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居三年，老而病，猶乞進用。

translations.literal: After three years in office, old and ill, he still begged for further employment.
translations.idiomatic: After three years, though aged and ill, he still petitioned for promotion.

sentences.zh: 神宗薄之，詔提舉成都玉局觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong thought little of this and ordered him to superintend the Jade Bureau Abbey of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong held him in low regard and posted him to superintend the Jade Bureau Abbey in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 從臣外祠自此始。

translations.literal: From this began the practice of outside abbey posts for former court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the practice of assigning retired court ministers to outside Taoist abbeys.

sentences.zh: 遂以尚書右丞致仕。

translations.literal: He then retired as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He finally retired with the title Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 吳中復

translations.literal: Wu Zhongfu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongfu

sentences.zh: 吳中復，字仲庶，興國永興人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhongfu, styled Zhongshu, was a native of Yongxing in Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongfu, courtesy name Zhongshu, came from Yongxing in Xingguo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 父仲舉，仕李煜為池陽令。

translations.literal: His father Zhongju served Li Yu as magistrate of Chiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongju had served Li Yu as magistrate of Chiyang.

sentences.zh: 曹彬平江南，仲舉嘗殺彬所招使者。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin pacified Jiangnan, Zhongju had once killed an envoy whom Bin had recruited.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin conquered Jiangnan, Zhongju had killed an envoy Bin had sent to win him over.

sentences.zh: 城陷，彬執之，仲舉曰：「世祿李氏，國亡而死，職也。」

translations.literal: When the city fell, Bin seized him; Zhongju said: "I received salary from the Li house; when the state perished I should die—that is duty."
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, Bin captured him. Zhongju said, "I drew stipend from the House of Li; when the realm fell, death was my duty."

sentences.zh: 彬義而不殺。

translations.literal: Bin regarded this as righteous and did not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Bin honored his integrity and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 中復進士及第，知峨眉縣。

translations.literal: Zhongfu passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Emei County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Emei County.

sentences.zh: 邊夷民事淫祠太盛，中復悉廢之。

translations.literal: Among frontier tribes civil affairs and excessive shrines were too numerous; Zhongfu abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples maintained far too many licentious shrines; Zhongfu abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 廉於居官，代還，不載一物。

translations.literal: He was incorruptible in office; when replaced and returning, he carried not a single thing.
translations.idiomatic: Incorruptible in office, he returned from his post without a single personal possession.

sentences.zh: 通判潭州，御史中丞孫抃薦為監察御史，初不相識也。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Tan Prefecture, Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Bian recommended him as Supervising Censor—they had not known each other before.
translations.idiomatic: While vice prefect of Tan Prefecture, he was recommended for Supervising Censor by Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Bian, though the two had never met.

sentences.zh: 或問之，抃曰：「昔人恥為呈身御史，今豈有識面臺官耶？」

translations.literal: When someone asked about this, Bian said: "Men of old were ashamed to become censors by presenting themselves; how could there today be censors who know their superiors by sight?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Bian replied, "Men of old scorned becoming censors by currying favor—would a censor today be chosen because he had made the acquaintance of his chief?"

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Censor-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Censor-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 彈宰相梁適，仁宗曰：「馬遵亦言之矣。」

translations.literal: He impeached Chancellor Liang Shi; Emperor Renzong said: "Ma Zun has also spoken of this."
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Chancellor Liang Shi. Emperor Renzong said, "Ma Zun has raised this as well."

sentences.zh: 且問中復曰：「唐自天寶後治亂分，何也？」

translations.literal: And he asked Zhongfu: "After the Tianbao era of Tang, order and disorder divided—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he asked Zhongfu, "After Tang's Tianbao era, peace and chaos parted ways—why?"

sentences.zh: 中復歷引姚、宋、九齡、林甫、國忠用舍以對。

translations.literal: Zhongfu in sequence cited the employment and dismissal of Yao, Song, Jiuling, Linfu, and Guozhong in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu answered by tracing how the rise and fall of Yao Chong, Song Jing, Zhang Jiuling, Li Linfu, and Yang Guozhong had turned the age.

sentences.zh: 適罷，中復亦通判虔州，未至，復還臺。

translations.literal: Shi was dismissed; Zhongfu also became vice prefect of Qian Prefecture, but before arriving he was returned to the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shi was removed; Zhongfu was posted as vice prefect of Qian Prefecture, but before he arrived he was recalled to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 富弼主李仲昌開六塔河，內臣劉恢密告所斷岡與國姓上名同，賈昌朝陰助之，欲以搖弼。

translations.literal: Fu Bi championed Li Zhongchang's project to open the Six Pagoda River; eunuch Liu Hui secretly reported that a ridge cut there shared the characters of the dynastic surname and personal name; Jia Changchao secretly aided this, wishing to shake Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi backed Li Zhongchang's plan to open the Six Pagoda River. Eunuch Liu Hui secretly claimed a ridge to be cut bore the characters of the imperial surname and given name; Jia Changchao quietly abetted him, hoping to unseat Bi.

sentences.zh: 詔中復往治，促行甚急。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhongfu to investigate; he was urged to depart with great haste.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Zhongfu to investigate, with orders to hurry.

sentences.zh: 中復言：「獄起奸臣，非盛世所宜有。」

translations.literal: Zhongfu said: "A case arising from treacherous ministers is not what a flourishing age should have."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu declared, "A prosecution born of treacherous ministers ill befits a flourishing age."

sentences.zh: 馳至，較其名，乃趙征村也，亦無岡勢，獄以故得止。

translations.literal: He galloped there, compared the name, and it was Zhao Zheng Village; there was also no ridge formation, and the case therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He rode hard to the site, checked the place-name—it was Zhao Zheng Village, with no ominous ridge—and the case collapsed.

sentences.zh: 又彈宰相劉沆，沆罷。

translations.literal: He again impeached Chancellor Liu Hang, and Hang was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Chancellor Liu Hang as well, and Hang was removed.

sentences.zh: 改右司諫，同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Remonstrance Officer and Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Remonstrance Officer and Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷御史知雜事、戶部副使，擢天章閣待制，知澤州、瀛州，移河東都轉運使，進龍圖閣直學士、知江寧府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Censor with Miscellaneous Duties and Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Revenue, elevated to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall, served as prefect of Ze and Ying Prefectures, moved to Transport Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit, and advanced to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Supervising Censor with Miscellaneous Duties and Vice Commissioner of Revenue to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall, governing Ze and Ying Prefectures, then Hedong transport, then Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 郵兵苦巡轄官苛刻，縶而鞭之。

translations.literal: Postal soldiers suffered under the harshness of patrol officers and bound and whipped them.
translations.idiomatic: Postal couriers, tormented by harsh patrol officers, seized and flogged their overseers.

sentences.zh: 獄具，法不至死，中復以便宜戮首惡，流其餘，入奏為令。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, by law death was not reached; Zhongfu by expedient executed the ringleaders and exiled the rest, then entered court and made this a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The law did not require death, but Zhongfu summarily executed the ringleaders, exiled the rest, and memorialized to make this precedent.

sentences.zh: 歷成德軍、成都府、永興軍。

translations.literal: He successively served at the Chengde Army, Chengdu Prefecture, and Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed the Chengde Army, Chengdu Prefecture, and the Yongxing Army in succession.

sentences.zh: 河北行青苗法，使者至，將先下州縣。

translations.literal: In Hebei the Green Sprouts Law was implemented; when the envoy arrived, he wished first to impose it on prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Green Sprouts Law reached Hebei, the imperial envoy meant to roll it out through prefectures and counties first.

sentences.zh: 中復檄之曰：「斂散自有期，今先事擾之，何也？」

translations.literal: Zhongfu wrote in dispatch: "Collection and distribution have their fixed seasons—why disturb matters beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu wrote back, "Grain is levied and released on fixed schedules—why stir trouble ahead of time?"

sentences.zh: 拒不聽，且以報。

translations.literal: He refused to obey and also reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: He refused compliance and reported the matter upward.

sentences.zh: 安撫司韓琦方疏諫青苗，錄其語以上。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Han Qi was then memorializing against the Green Sprouts Law and copied out his words to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Han Qi was already remonstrating against the Green Sprouts Law and forwarded Zhongfu's words to court.

sentences.zh: 熙寧倂省郡邑，以永康為縣，中復言：「永康控威、茂，不可廢。」

translations.literal: In the Xining era commanderies and counties were merged, and Yongkang was made a county; Zhongfu said: "Yongkang controls Wei and Mao—it cannot be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: During Xining's consolidation of districts, Yongkang was reduced to a county. Zhongfu argued, "Yongkang guards Wei and Mao—it must not be abolished."

sentences.zh: 其後因夷竟復之。

translations.literal: Later, because of the tribes, it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later, owing to the tribal peoples, it was restored.

sentences.zh: 關內大旱，民多流亡。

translations.literal: Within the passes there was great drought, and many people fled.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought within the passes drove many people to flee.

sentences.zh: 中復請加賑恤，執政惡之，遣使往視，謂為不實，削一階，提舉玉隆觀。

translations.literal: Zhongfu requested increased relief; the chief ministers disliked this, sent an envoy to inspect, said it was untrue, reduced him one rank, and assigned him to superintend the Yulong Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu asked for greater relief; the chief ministers resented it, sent investigators who declared his report false, stripped him of one rank, and posted him to superintend the Yulong Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知荊南，坐過用公使酒，免。

translations.literal: He was raised to govern Jingnan but was dismissed for excessive use of official entertainment wine.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to govern Jingnan, he was dismissed for overspending official entertainment wine.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 中復樂易簡約，好周人之急，士大夫稱之。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was cheerful, easy, and simple, delighting to relieve others' urgency; scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Easygoing and plain in habit, he loved to rescue others in distress, and the literati held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 從孫擇仁。

translations.literal: His collateral descendant Zerén.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral descendant was Zerén.

sentences.zh: 從孫 擇仁

translations.literal: Collateral descendant Zerén
translations.idiomatic: Zerén, a Collateral Descendant

sentences.zh: 擇仁，字智夫，以父任，為開封雍丘主簿。

translations.literal: Zerén, styled Zhifu, entered office through his father's position as chief clerk of Yongqiu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zerén, courtesy name Zhifu, entered service through yin privilege as chief clerk of Yongqiu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，金水河堤壞，十六縣皆選屬庀役，得詣朝堂白事。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era the Jinshui River dike broke, and sixteen counties each chose subordinates to oversee the labor, gaining audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, when the Jinshui River dike failed, sixteen counties each dispatched subordinates to manage corvée labor and gain access to the court.

sentences.zh: 宰相范純仁獨異之，曰：「簿領中乃有是人邪？」

translations.literal: Chancellor Fan Chunren alone was struck by him and said: "In ledger work there is actually such a man?"
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Fan Chunren alone took notice and exclaimed, "Can such a man really be found among ledger clerks?"

sentences.zh: 建中靖國初，畿內饑，多盜，以擇仁知太康縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong Jingguo era, famine within the capital region bred many bandits; Zerén was appointed magistrate of Taikang County.
translations.idiomatic: When famine and banditry spread through the capital region at the opening of the Jianzhong Jingguo era, Zerén was made magistrate of Taikang County.

sentences.zh: 始至，召令賊曹曰：「民窮而盜，非天性也，我以靜鎮之。

translations.literal: On first arriving, he summoned the magistrate of the bandit bureau and said: "When the people are poor they steal—it is not their nature; I will calm them by stillness.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he told the bandit-catchers, "Poverty drives men to theft—it is not inborn nature. I shall govern through calm restraint.

sentences.zh: 若亡命椎埋故犯，我一切誅之，毋得貸。」

translations.literal: If desperate outlaws deliberately commit capital crimes, I will execute them all without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: But hardened outlaws who kill for gain will all be put to death without mercy."

sentences.zh: 群盜相戒不入境。

translations.literal: The bandits mutually warned one another not to enter the county.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits warned one another to stay out of his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 中貴人譚稹奴犯法，按致於理。

translations.literal: A favored eunuch's slave, Tan Zhen's, broke the law; Zerén investigated and brought him to justice.
translations.idiomatic: When a favored eunuch Tan Zhen's slave broke the law, Zerén prosecuted him to the letter.

sentences.zh: 稹羞恚造譖，徽宗召戶部郎中宋喬年往鞫。

translations.literal: Tan, shamed and enraged, fabricated slander; Emperor Huizong summoned Ministry of Revenue Director Song Qiaonian to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Tan fabricated charges, and Huizong sent Ministry of Revenue Director Song Qiaonian to investigate.

sentences.zh: 喬年，伉吏也，疾驅至。

translations.literal: Qiaonian was a stern official and galloped there in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiaonian was a hard-driving official and raced to the county.

sentences.zh: 候者惶遽入白，擇仁著衣冠坐廡下。

translations.literal: The attendant, alarmed, rushed in to report; Zerén dressed in cap and robes and sat in the corridor.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant panicked and announced him; Zerén sat in full official dress in the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 喬年慮囚擿隱，剔抉帑庾出入，不能得毫毛罪，乃歸傳舍。

translations.literal: Qiaonian, fearing hidden guilt among prisoners, picked through treasury receipts and expenditures but could not find the slightest crime, and returned to the post station.
translations.idiomatic: Song tore through the jail and treasury records hunting for hidden guilt but found not a thread of offense, and withdrew to his lodging.

sentences.zh: 擇仁上謁，喬年迎笑曰：「所以來，為察君罪，顧乃得一奇士，吾今薦君矣。」

translations.literal: Zerén paid a visit; Qiaonian greeted him with a smile and said: "I came to inspect your crimes, yet instead found an extraordinary man—I shall now recommend you."
translations.idiomatic: When Zerén called on him, Song smiled and said, "I came to catch you in wrongdoing, but found an uncommon man instead. I mean to recommend you."

sentences.zh: 居數日，召詣闕。

translations.literal: After several days he was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was summoned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 方有事青唐，擢熙河路轉運判官，即以直秘閣為副使，從招討使王厚領兵深入，克蘭、廓城柵十三。

translations.literal: When Qing Tang was under campaign, he was promoted to Transport Assessor of the Xihe Circuit, then with Directorship of the Secret Archive made Vice Commissioner, following the Pacification Commissioner Wang Hou deep in with troops and capturing thirteen forts at Lan and Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: During operations in Qing Tang he rose to Transport Assessor of the Xihe Circuit, then Vice Commissioner with Directorship of the Secret Archive, accompanying Pacification Commissioner Wang Hou deep into enemy country to capture thirteen forts at Lan and Kuo.

sentences.zh: 加龍圖，進集賢殿修撰，為京畿都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was given the Dragon Diagram title, advanced to Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, and made Transport Commissioner of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: He received the Dragon Diagram designation, became Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, and Transport Commissioner of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 鄭州城惡，受命更築之。

translations.literal: The walls of Zheng Prefecture were poor; he received orders to rebuild them.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Prefecture's walls were crumbling, and he was ordered to rebuild them.

sentences.zh: 或讒於帝曰：「新城雜以沙土，反不如故，且速圮。」

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to the emperor, saying: "The new walls mixed with sand and soil are worse than the old and will quickly collapse."
translations.idiomatic: A detractor told the emperor, "The new walls are adulterated with sand and worse than before—they will soon fall."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，密遣取塊城上，緘以來，令衛卒三投之，堅緻如削鐵，讒不能售。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, secretly sent men to take a block from the wall, sealed and brought it; he ordered guard soldiers to throw it three times—it was dense as carved iron, and the slander could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor secretly had a wall block sealed and sent to court; three throws by guard soldiers showed iron-hard density, and the slander failed.

sentences.zh: 遂拜戶部侍郎兼知開封府。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 故事，尹以三日聽訟，右曹吏十輩列庭下，自占姓名，一人云：「某人送某獄，某人當杖，某人去」，而尹無所可否。

translations.literal: By precedent, the prefect heard cases on the third day; ten clerks of the right bureau lined up below the hall, each stating his name; one would say, "So-and-so sent to such-and-such prison, so-and-so deserves the rod, so-and-so dismissed," and the prefect neither affirmed nor denied.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the prefect heard cases every third day while ten right-bureau clerks lined the courtyard, calling out names and dispositions—"Send X to such-and-such prison, beat Y, release Z"—while the prefect assented to nothing.

sentences.zh: 有竇鑒者，以捕盜寵，官諸司使，服金帶。

translations.literal: There was one Dou Jian, favored for catching bandits, holding the office of Commissioner of Various Offices and wearing a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: One Dou Jian, a favorite for catching thieves, held rank as Commissioner of Various Offices and wore a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 擇仁視事，狃舊態來前，叱而械諸獄，一府大驚。

translations.literal: When Zerén took office, Jian, accustomed to the old ways, came forward; Zerén shouted at him and shackled him in prison—the whole prefecture was greatly shocked.
translations.idiomatic: When Zerén took office, Dou Jian approached as of old habit; Zerén rebuked him and had him shackled in jail, stunning the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賣珠人居民貨久不返，度事急，匿宦官楊戩第，擇仁跡取之，竄於遠。

translations.literal: A pearl merchant lent goods to a resident long without return; fearing urgency, he hid in eunuch Yang Kan's residence; Zerén traced and took him, and exiled him far away.
translations.idiomatic: A pearl merchant whose goods a resident long refused to return hid in eunuch Yang Kan's house when pressed; Zerén tracked him down and banished him far away.

sentences.zh: 戩中以事，出為顯謨閣直學士、知熙州，從永興軍。

translations.literal: Kan reported the matter, and Zerén was sent out as Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Instruction and prefect of Xi Prefecture, then attached to the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan lodged a complaint, and Zerén was posted out as Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Instruction and prefect of Xi Prefecture, later attached to the Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 走馬承受藍從熙言其擅改茶法，奪職，免。

translations.literal: Palace courier Lan Congxi reported that he had arbitrarily changed the tea law; his office was stripped and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace courier Lan Congxi accused him of altering the tea law on his own authority; he was stripped of office and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 再閱歲，以徽猷閣待制領江淮發運，還直學士、知渭州。

translations.literal: After another year he was made Court Gentleman of the Hall of Imperial Instruction to head Huai-Hai grain transport, then restored as Direct Academician and prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he headed Huai-Hai grain transport as Court Gentleman of the Hall of Imperial Instruction, then returned as Direct Academician and prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以病提舉崇福宮，起知青州，不克拜，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was assigned to superintend the Chongfu Palace; raised to govern Qing Prefecture, he could not assume the post and died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to superintendence of the Chongfu Palace; though recalled to govern Qing Prefecture, he could not take up the post and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 陳薦，字彥升，邢州沙河人。

translations.literal: Chen Jian, styled Yansheng, was a native of Shahe in Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jian, courtesy name Yansheng, came from Shahe in Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為華陽尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became marshal of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as marshal of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 盜殺人，棄屍民田。

translations.literal: Bandits killed a man and abandoned the corpse in a civilian's field.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits murdered a man and dumped the body in a farmer's field.

sentences.zh: 薦出驗，有以移屍告者。

translations.literal: Jian went out to examine the body; someone reported that the corpse had been moved.
translations.idiomatic: Jian went to examine the corpse, and someone reported that the body had been moved.

sentences.zh: 田主又殺其母。

translations.literal: The field owner had also killed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The field owner had also killed his own mother.

sentences.zh: 縣欲聞致殺二人，以逭薦失盜之責。

translations.literal: The county wished to report two killings together to escape Jian's responsibility for losing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The county wanted to report two murders together to shield Jian from blame for failing to catch the bandits.

sentences.zh: 薦不可，曰：「焉有誣人以自貰者邪！」

translations.literal: Jian would not agree and said: "How could there be one who falsely accuses others to reward himself!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused, saying, "Who would frame an innocent man to clear himself?"

sentences.zh: 已而獲盜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the bandits were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were captured soon after.

sentences.zh: 從韓琦定州、河東幕府。

translations.literal: He followed Han Qi in the staffs of Ding Prefecture and the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served on Han Qi's staffs at Ding Prefecture and in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 性木強簡澹，獨琦知之最深，每語人曰：「廉於進，勇於退，嫌疑間毫髮不處，與人交久而不變，如彥升者，無幾也。」

translations.literal: By nature obstinate, plain, and detached, Qi alone knew him deepest and often told others: "Frugal in advancing, bold in retreating, not placing himself within a hair's breadth of suspicion, unchanged in long association—few are like Yansheng."
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn, plain, and reserved, he was known best by Han Qi, who often said, "Frugal in ambition, bold in withdrawal, never touching the shadow of suspicion, steadfast through long acquaintance—men like Yansheng are rare."

sentences.zh: 琦輔政，薦為秘閣校理、判登聞檢院、知太常禮院。

translations.literal: When Qi assisted in government, Jian was recommended as Collator of the Secret Archive, judge of the Petition Office, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi entered the chief ministry, Jian was made Collator of the Secret Archive, judge of the Petition Office, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 英宗諸王出閣，選為記室參軍，直集賢院。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong's princes left the palace, Jian was chosen as Recorder and attached to the Hall for Treasuring Literature.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong's sons left the inner palace, Jian was chosen as Recorder and attached to the Hall for Treasuring Literature.

sentences.zh: 潁王為皇太子，加右諭德；

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ying became crown prince, Jian was made Right Mentor;
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong was named crown prince, Jian received the post of Right Mentor;

sentences.zh: 王即位，拜天章閣待制，進知制誥、知諫院。

translations.literal: when the prince ascended the throne, Jian was appointed Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall, then promoted to Drafter of Edicts and Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: when that prince ascended the throne, Jian became Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall, then Drafter of Edicts and Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 薛向首謀取橫山，功不成，薦請以漢王恢之罪罪向。

translations.literal: Xue Xiang first plotted to take Hengshan; the effort failed, and Jian requested that Xue be punished with the crime of Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiang had first plotted to seize Hengshan and failed; Jian asked that he be punished under the precedent of Wang Hui's crime.

sentences.zh: 楊繪論曾公亮用人不當，言既行而遷侍讀，罷諫職。

translations.literal: Yang Hui discussed Zeng Gongliang's improper appointments; after his words were acted on he was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting and removed from remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui criticized Zeng Gongliang's appointments; though his remonstrance was heeded, he was moved to Reader-in-Waiting and stripped of remonstrance office.

sentences.zh: 薦曰：「此乃宰相欲杜繪言爾，所言是，宜責宰相。」

translations.literal: Jian said: "This is simply the chancellor wishing to silence Hui's speech; what he said was right—the chancellor should be blamed."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "The chancellor only wants to silence Yang Hui. Hui was right—the chancellor should bear the blame."

sentences.zh: 疏入不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went in unanswered.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣直學士、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Transport Commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Transport Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 河決棗強，水官議於恩、冀、深、瀛之間築堤三百六十里，期一月就功，役丁夫八萬。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke at Zaoqiang; water officials proposed building dikes for three hundred sixty li between En, Ji, Shen, and Ying, expecting completion in one month with eighty thousand corvée laborers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst at Zaoqiang, water officials proposed three hundred sixty li of dikes between En, Ji, Shen, and Ying, to be finished in one month with eighty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 薦曰：「河未能為數州害，民力方困，願以歲月為之。」

translations.literal: Jian said: "The river cannot yet harm several prefectures; the people's strength is already exhausted—I wish it done over months."
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "The river is not yet a grave threat to several prefectures, and the people are exhausted. Let the work proceed over time."

sentences.zh: 還，判流內銓、太常寺。

translations.literal: On return he judged the Flowing Within Bureau and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he judged the Flowing Within Bureau and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 議學校貢舉法，請會三年貢士數均之諸路，計口察孝廉如漢制。

translations.literal: When school and examination laws were debated, he requested that three years' quota of presented scholars be averaged among circuits and that filial and incorrupt men be selected by population as in Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Debating school and examination reform, he proposed averaging three years of examination quotas across circuits and selecting filial and incorrupt men by population after the Han model.

sentences.zh: 權主管御史臺，言李定匿所生母喪，不宜為御史。

translations.literal: Acting as chief of the Censorate, he said Li Ding had concealed mourning for his biological mother and was unfit to be censor.
translations.idiomatic: Acting chief of the Censorate, he argued that Li Ding, having concealed mourning for his birth mother, was unfit to serve as censor.

sentences.zh: 罷臺事。

translations.literal: He was removed from Censorate duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his Censorate responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 又以議典禮不合，出知蔡州。

translations.literal: Again, because his views on ritual did not accord, he was sent out as prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because his ritual opinions did not accord with court policy, he was sent out as prefect of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召為寶文閣學士兼侍讀，進資政殿學士。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and Reader-in-Waiting, and advanced to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and Reader-in-Waiting, then advanced to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Virtue.

sentences.zh: 屢求退，以為本州，命兩省燕餞資善堂。

translations.literal: Repeatedly requesting retirement, he was granted his home prefecture; the two departments were ordered to give a banquet for him at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated requests to retire, he was granted his home prefecture, and both departments were ordered to banquet him at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 擢其子厚御史臺主簿。

translations.literal: His son Hou was promoted to chief clerk of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The court elevated his son Hou to chief clerk of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Before long he was assigned to superintend the Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned to superintend the Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-nine and was posthumously given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 王獵，字得之，長垣人。

translations.literal: Wang Lie, styled Dezhi, was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lie, courtesy name Dezhi, came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 累應進士不第，乃治生積錢，既而歎曰：「此敗吾志也。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly failed the jinshi examination, then pursued livelihood and amassed money; afterward he sighed and said: "This ruins my aspiration."
translations.idiomatic: After repeated failure at the jinshi examinations, he went into trade and amassed money, then sighed, "This destroys my purpose in life."

sentences.zh: 悉以班諸親族。

translations.literal: He distributed it all among his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He gave it all away to his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 慶曆用兵，詔求遺逸，范仲淹薦之，得出身為永興藍田主薄。

translations.literal: During the Qingli military campaigns an edict sought hidden talent; Fan Zhongyan recommended him, and he received initial appointment as chief clerk of Lantian in Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qingli campaigns prompted a search for hidden talent, Fan Zhongyan recommended him, and he entered service as chief clerk of Lantian in Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 府使之掌學，諸生有犯法者，獵自責數，以為教之不至，屏出之府。

translations.literal: The prefecture ordered him to manage the school; when a student violated the law, Lie blamed himself and counted his faults, thinking teaching had not reached far enough, and expelled the student from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture put him in charge of the school; when a student broke the law, Lie blamed himself for poor instruction and expelled the boy from the academy.

sentences.zh: 帥意其私，捕生下獄，獵前白曰：「此特年少不率教爾。

translations.literal: The commander suspected private motive, arrested the student and imprisoned him; Lie stepped forward and said: "This is simply a youth not following instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor suspected favoritism, jailed the student, and Lie stepped forward: "This is only a young man who would not heed his teachers.

sentences.zh: 致於理，不足以益美化，恐適貽士類辱。」

translations.literal: Bringing him to law does not enough increase civilizing beauty and may only bring shame on scholars."
translations.idiomatic: Prosecution will not enhance moral cultivation—it will only disgrace the scholar class."

sentences.zh: 帥悟而喜曰：「吾慮初不及此。」

translations.literal: The commander understood and said with pleasure: "My thought at first did not reach this."
translations.idiomatic: The governor saw the point and exclaimed, "I never thought that far."

sentences.zh: 即釋生而待獵加敬。

translations.literal: He immediately released the student and treated Lie with added respect.
translations.idiomatic: He released the student at once and treated Lie with new respect.

sentences.zh: 徙林慮令，縣依山，俗以搜田為生，不知學。

translations.literal: Transferred to magistrate of Linlu County—the county lay against mountains, and custom made a living from hunting fields, not knowing learning.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of mountainous Linlu County, where people lived by hunting and knew nothing of learning,

sentences.zh: 獵立孔子廟，擇秀民誨之。

translations.literal: Lie established a temple to Confucius and selected outstanding commoners to instruct.
translations.idiomatic: he built a Confucian temple and chose promising locals to teach.

sentences.zh: 漢杜喬墓在境中，往奠謁，建祠其旁。

translations.literal: The tomb of Han's Du Qiao was within the border; he went to offer sacrifice and built a shrine beside it.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed at the tomb of the Han official Du Qiao within his jurisdiction and built a shrine beside it.

sentences.zh: 居官無絲髮擾，吏民愛信，共目為清長官。

translations.literal: In office he gave not the slightest disturbance; officials and people loved and trusted him, together calling him the upright senior official.
translations.idiomatic: He never troubled the people in the least; officials and commoners loved and trusted him, calling him the upright magistrate.

sentences.zh: 入為吳王潭王宮教授、睦親廣親宅講書、諸王侍講。

translations.literal: He entered court as instructor in the palaces of the Princes of Wu and Tan, lecturer at the Hall of Harmonious Kinship and Broad Kinship, and Lecturer to the Princes.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as instructor to the Princes of Wu and Tan, lecturer at the halls of imperial kinship, and Lecturer to the Princes.

sentences.zh: 凡在京藩十二年，宗室無高卑少長，各得其歡如一日。

translations.literal: Altogether twelve years in the capital princely establishment—the imperial clan, high or low, young or old, each found his pleasure as in one day.
translations.idiomatic: For twelve years in the capital princely establishment, clansmen high and low, young and old, all found equal delight in his company.

sentences.zh: 英宗在邸，尊禮之；

translations.literal: When Yingzong was in his princely residence, he honored Lie;
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong, while still in his princely residence, honored him;

sentences.zh: 入為皇子，即拜說書；

translations.literal: when he entered as crown prince, Lie was immediately appointed Lecturer;
translations.idiomatic: when Yingzong became crown prince, Lie was immediately made Lecturer;

sentences.zh: 及即位，拜天章閣待制兼侍講。

translations.literal: when he ascended the throne, Lie was appointed Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: and when he took the throne, Lie became Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 方議濮王稱，以問獵，獵不可。

translations.literal: When the title of the Prince of Pu was under debate, the emperor asked Lie, and Lie disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: When court debated titles for the Prince of Pu, the emperor consulted Lie, who disapproved.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「王待侍講厚，亦持此說邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The prince treats the Lecturer generously—do you also hold this view?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "The prince has treated you generously—do you still hold this view?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣荷皇恩厚，不敢以非禮名號加於王，所以報王也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant bears thick imperial grace and dares not add an unorthodox title to the prince—that is how I repay the prince."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I owe deep imperial grace and dare not attach an improper title to the prince—that is how I repay his kindness."

sentences.zh: 帝大悟，自是不復議。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly understood and from then did not debate further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw clearly and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 以疾請謝事，不許。

translations.literal: Because of illness he requested to leave office; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to request retirement, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 疾愈入見，帝喜曰：「侍講乃欲舍朕去乎？」

translations.literal: When recovered he entered audience; the emperor said with pleasure: "Does the Lecturer mean to leave Us?"
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered and attended audience, the emperor said warmly, "Lecturer, would you abandon Us?"

sentences.zh: 神宗立，進龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Lie was promoted to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Lie was promoted to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 求知襄州，未行，改滑州。

translations.literal: He requested to govern Xiang Prefecture; before departing he was changed to Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He sought appointment at Xiang Prefecture but was transferred to Hua Prefecture before he could depart.

sentences.zh: 自工部郎中為本曹侍郎致仕，給全奉。

translations.literal: From Director of the Ministry of Works he retired as Vice Minister of the same ministry, granted full salary.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from Director of the Ministry of Works as Vice Minister of that ministry, with full salary continued.

sentences.zh: 後八年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: Eight years later he died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died eight years later at eighty.

sentences.zh: 詔賻絹千匹，官其二孫，賜家人冠帔，人以為寵。

translations.literal: An edict granted one thousand bolts of silk as funeral gifts, gave office to two grandsons, and bestowed caps and sashes on the family—people regarded this as favor.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted a thousand bolts of silk, office to two grandsons, and caps and sashes to the family—a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 孫思恭

translations.literal: Sun Sigong
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sigong

sentences.zh: 孫思恭，字彥先，登州人。

translations.literal: Sun Sigong, styled Yanxian, was a native of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sigong, courtesy name Yanxian, came from Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢第後，即遭父喪，不肯復從官，二十年間才三書吏考。

translations.literal: After passing the examination he immediately suffered his father's mourning and would not again follow office; in twenty years he recorded only three clerk evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examinations he entered mourning for his father and refused further service, recording only three clerk evaluations in twenty years.

sentences.zh: 為宛丘令，轉運使以水災時調春夫，爭弗得，乃棄官去。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Wanqiu, the transport commissioner requisitioned spring corvée during flood season; he could not prevail in dispute and abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Wanqiu he quarreled with the transport commissioner over spring corvée during floods, failed to prevail, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 吳奎薦其學行，補國子直講，加秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Wu Kui recommended his learning and conduct; he was appointed Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education and added as Collator of the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kui recommended his scholarship and conduct, and he became Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education and Collator of the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 事神宗藩邸為說書，又為侍講、直集賢院。

translations.literal: He served in Prince Shenzong's princely residence as Lecturer, then as Reader-in-Waiting and attached to the Hall for Treasuring Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He served Shenzong's princely household as Lecturer, then as Reader-in-Waiting attached to the Hall for Treasuring Literature.

sentences.zh: 以居中都久，力請補外，王奏留之。

translations.literal: Because he had long lived in the capital, he strongly requested an outside post; the prince memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: After long residence in the capital he begged for an outside post, but the prince memorialized to keep him.

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢天章閣待制。

translations.literal: When the prince ascended the throne, he was elevated to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, he was elevated to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall.

sentences.zh: 思恭性不忤物，犯而不校，篤於事上。

translations.literal: Sigong by nature did not oppose others, and though offended did not contend; he was devoted in serving his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Easy-natured and uncontentious even when wronged, he was devoted in service to his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 有所見，必密疏以聞。

translations.literal: When he had a view, he always reported it in a secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he observed, he reported in secret memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝亦間訪以政。

translations.literal: The emperor also occasionally consulted him on government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also occasionally sought his counsel on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修初不知思恭，修出政府，思恭盡力救解。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu at first did not know Sigong; when Xiu left the government, Sigong exerted himself to rescue and exonerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu did not know him at first; when Xiu fell from power, Sigong worked tirelessly to clear him.

sentences.zh: 出知江寧府、鄧州，以疾移單州，管幹南京留司御史臺。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Jiangning and Deng Prefectures, he moved because of illness to Shan Prefecture and managed the Nanjing branch of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Jiangning and Deng Prefectures, he moved to Shan Prefecture for illness and managed the Nanjing branch of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 思恭精關氏《易》，尤妙於《大衍》。

translations.literal: Sigong was expert in Master Guan's 《Changes》, and especially skilled in the 《Great Evolution》.
translations.idiomatic: Sigong mastered Master Guan's 《Book of Changes》 and excelled above all in the 《Great Evolution》.

sentences.zh: 嘗修天文院渾儀，著《堯年至熙寧長曆》，近世曆數之學，未有能及之者。

translations.literal: He once repaired the armillary sphere of the Astronomical Bureau and wrote 《Long Calendar from the Era of Yao to Xining》; in recent calendrical studies none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Astronomical Bureau armillary sphere and wrote 《Long Calendar from the Era of Yao to Xining》; in calendrical science of his age none surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 周孟陽

translations.literal: Zhou Mengyang
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mengyang

sentences.zh: 周孟陽，字春卿，其先成都人，徙海陵。

translations.literal: Zhou Mengyang, styled Chunqing, his ancestors were natives of Chengdu and moved to Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mengyang, courtesy name Chunqing, was descended from Chengdu people who had moved to Hailing.

sentences.zh: 醇謹夷緩。

translations.literal: Pure, cautious, mild, and unhurried.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure, cautious, mild, and unhurried in manner.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為潭王宮教授、諸王府記室。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became instructor in the Prince of Tan's palace and Recorder in various princely households.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he taught in the Prince of Tan's palace and served as Recorder in various princely households.

sentences.zh: 英宗居環列，以其質厚，禮重之，會除知宗正寺，力辭，凡上十八表，皆孟陽為文。

translations.literal: When Yingzong lived among the princes, because of his solid character he was honored; when appointment as Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan was imminent, he forcefully declined—altogether eighteen memorials, all drafted by Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong, living among the princes, honored him for his solid character; when appointment as Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan loomed, Yingzong forcefully declined in eighteen memorials—all drafted by Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 又從容陳古事以諷，英宗悚然起拜；

translations.literal: Mengyang also calmly cited ancient precedents by way of admonition; Yingzong started in alarm and rose to bow;
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang also gently cited ancient precedents in admonition, and Yingzong started up in alarm and bowed;

sentences.zh: 及為皇子，愈堅臥不出。

translations.literal: when he became crown prince, he lay ill and would not come out all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: when made crown prince he lay abed and refused all the more firmly to emerge.

sentences.zh: 孟陽入見臥內，勸之曰：「天子知太尉賢，參以天人之助，乃發德音。

translations.literal: Mengyang entered to see him in the sickroom and urged: "The Son of Heaven knows the Grand Marshal is worthy and, joined with Heaven and man's aid, has issued virtuous words.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang entered the sickroom and urged him, "The emperor knows Your Highness is worthy and, with Heaven's and men's support, has issued a virtuous summons.

sentences.zh: 何為堅拒如此？」

translations.literal: Why resist so firmly?"
translations.idiomatic: Why resist so stubbornly?"

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「非敢徼福，以避禍也。」

translations.literal: Yingzong said: "It is not that I dare seek fortune—I seek to avoid calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong replied, "I do not seek fortune—I seek to avoid disaster."

sentences.zh: 孟陽曰：「今已有此跡，設固辭不拜，使中人別有所奉，遂得燕安無患乎？」

translations.literal: Mengyang said: "Now this trace already exists; suppose you firmly decline and do not accept—if eunuchs then set up another candidate, could you then dwell in ease without worry?"
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang said, "The trail is already laid. If you refuse the throne and eunuchs advance another candidate, will you then live untroubled?"

sentences.zh: 時中使趣召十輩，又命宗諤傾一宮往請，不能動，及是，意乃決。

translations.literal: At the time ten batches of palace envoys urged summons; the emperor also ordered Zong'e to bring the whole palace to invite him—they could not move him; only then did his mind decide.
translations.idiomatic: Ten rounds of palace envoys had already pressed him; the emperor even sent Zong'e with the whole inner palace to plead—only then did Yingzong resolve to accept.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，命為皇子位說書，以嘗侍藩邸，固辭。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was ordered Lecturer to the crown prince's place; because he had once served the princely residence, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne, Mengyang was ordered Lecturer to the crown prince but declined, having already served the princely household.

sentences.zh: 加直秘閣、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: He was given Directorship of the Secret Archive and Associate Directorship of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He received Directorship of the Secret Archive and Associate Directorship of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 數引對，訪以時務。

translations.literal: Repeatedly summoned for audience, he was consulted on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly summoned to audience, he was consulted on affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 最後，召至隆儒殿，在邇英苑中，群臣未嘗至。

translations.literal: Finally he was summoned to the Hall of Elevating Confucianism, within the ErYing Garden—ministers had never reached it.
translations.idiomatic: At last he was summoned to the Hall of Elevating Confucianism in the ErYing Garden, a place no minister had entered before.

sentences.zh: 人疑且大用，帝亦諭以不次進擢意。

translations.literal: People suspected he would soon be greatly employed; the emperor also instructed him of intent to promote out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Observers suspected imminent high appointment; the emperor hinted at extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 孟陽稱他人，使代己，乃遷集賢殿修撰、同判太常寺兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Mengyang named another man to replace himself and was then transferred to Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, Associate Judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang recommended another to replace him and was transferred to Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, Associate Judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 神宗初立，入奏事，方升殿，帝望見慟哭，左右皆泣下。

translations.literal: When Shenzong first ascended the throne, Mengyang entered to report affairs; as he was ascending the hall the emperor saw him and wept bitterly, and those at left and right all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong first took the throne, Mengyang came to report affairs; the emperor saw him ascending the hall and wept, and attendants wept with him.

sentences.zh: 拜天章閣待制。

translations.literal: He was appointed Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 詔特官其婿及子孫二人，除其家負官緡錢數萬。

translations.literal: An edict specially gave office to his son-in-law and two descendants and remitted several tens of thousands in official money owed by his family.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially enfeoffed his son-in-law and two descendants and remitted tens of thousands of strings in official debt owed by his family.

sentences.zh: 楊繪，字元素，綿竹人。

translations.literal: Yang Hui, styled Yuansu, was a native of Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hui, courtesy name Yuansu, came from Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 少而奇警，讀書五行俱下，名聞西州。

translations.literal: Young and unusually sharp, in reading five lines at once he was famed throughout the western circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Precocious and brilliant, he read five lines at a glance and was famed throughout the western circuits.

sentences.zh: 進士上第，通判荊南。

translations.literal: He placed at the top of the jinshi list and became vice prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the jinshi list and served as vice prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 以集賢校理為開封推官，遇事迎刃而解，諸吏惟日不足，繪未午率沛然。

translations.literal: As Collator of the Hall for Treasuring Literature he became investigating officer of Kaifeng; matters met him and split apart, clerks daily lacked time, yet Hui before noon was always finished and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As Collator of the Hall for Treasuring Literature and Kaifeng investigating officer, he cut through cases effortlessly while clerks could not keep pace—yet Hui was always done before noon.

sentences.zh: 仁宗愛其才，欲超置侍從，執政見其年少，不用。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong loved his talent and wished to leap him into attendance on the throne; the chief ministers, seeing his youth, did not use him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong admired his talent and wished to leap him into close attendance, but chief ministers, deeming him too young, blocked the move.

sentences.zh: 以母老，請知眉州，徙興元府。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he requested to govern Mei Prefecture and was transferred to Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother aged, he sought Mei Prefecture and was transferred to Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吏請攝穿窬盜庫縑者，繪就視之，蹤跡不類人所出入，則曰：「我知之矣。」

translations.literal: Clerks requested he take charge of burglars who stole silk from the treasury; Hui went to view it—the tracks did not resemble human coming and going, and he said: "I know this."
translations.idiomatic: Clerks asked him to pursue burglars who stole treasury silk; Hui inspected the scene, saw tracks unlike human passage, and said, "I know the culprit."

sentences.zh: 呼戲沐猴者詰於庭，一訊具伏，府中服其明。

translations.literal: He summoned monkey trainers and questioned them in court; one interrogation and all confessed—the prefecture admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned monkey trainers to court; one interrogation produced full confession, and the prefecture marveled at his insight.

sentences.zh: 在郡獄無繫囚。

translations.literal: While in the prefecture there were no prisoners in jail.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure the prefectural jail held no prisoners.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，召修起居注、知制誥、知諫院。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was summoned to compile the Diary of Activity and Repose, draft edicts, and direct the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Hui was summoned to compile the imperial diary, draft edicts, and direct the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 詔遣內侍王中正、李舜舉等使陝西，繪言：「陛下新即位，天下拭目以觀初政。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched palace attendants Wang Zhongzheng, Li Shunju, and others as envoys to Shaanxi; Hui said: "Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne—the realm watches to see the first policies.
translations.idiomatic: When palace attendants Wang Zhongzheng and Li Shunju were dispatched to Shaanxi, Hui said, "Your Majesty has just ascended the throne; the realm watches your opening policies.

sentences.zh: 館閣、臺省之士，朝廷所素養者不之遣，顧獨遣中人乎？」

translations.literal: Men of the Pavilion and Secretariat whom the court has long cultivated are not sent—yet attendants alone are dispatched?"
translations.idiomatic: Scholars long cultivated in pavilion and secretariat posts are passed over—yet eunuchs alone are sent?"

sentences.zh: 向傳範安撫京東西路，繪請易之，以杜外戚干進之漸。

translations.literal: Xiang Chuanfan was pacification commissioner of the eastern and western capital circuits; Hui requested he be replaced to block the gradual encroachment of consort kin seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Chuanfan was made pacification commissioner of the eastern and western capital circuits, Hui asked that he be replaced to block consort kin from seeking office.

sentences.zh: 執政曰：「不然，傳範久領郡，有政聲，故使守鄆，非由外戚也。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers said: "It is not so—Chuanfan long governed prefectures with a reputation for good administration, therefore he was sent to guard Yan—not because of consort kin."
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers replied, "Chuanfan long governed with a good name—that is why he guards Yan, not through consort influence."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諫官言是，斯可窒異日妄求矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The remonstrance official is right—this can block reckless requests hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The remonstrator is right. This can choke off reckless petitions hereafter."

sentences.zh: 曾公亮請以其子判登聞鼓院，用所厚曾鞏為史官。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang requested that his son judge the Petition Drum Court and that Zeng Gong, whom he favored, be made historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang asked that his son judge the Petition Drum Court and that his protégé Zeng Gong become historiographer.

sentences.zh: 繪爭曰：「公亮持國，名器視如己物。

translations.literal: Hui contended: "Gongliang holds the state and treats offices and honors as his own possessions.
translations.idiomatic: Hui objected, "Gongliang treats the state as his private estate and offices as personal property.

sentences.zh: 向者公亮官越，占民田，為郡守繩治，時鞏父易占亦官越，深庇之。

translations.literal: Formerly when Gongliang was prefect of Yue he occupied civilian fields; a prefect punished him; at the time Gong's father Yi Zhan also held Yue and deeply sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was prefect of Yue he seized civilian land and was punished by a local governor; Gong's father Yi Zhan, then also in Yue, shielded him deeply.

sentences.zh: 用鞏，私也。」

translations.literal: Employing Gong is private motive."
translations.idiomatic: Appointing Zeng Gong is pure favoritism."

sentences.zh: 帝為寢其命。

translations.literal: The emperor shelved the order for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shelved the appointments.

sentences.zh: 繪亦解諫職，改兼侍讀，繪固辭，滕甫言於帝。

translations.literal: Hui also resigned remonstrance duties and was changed to concurrent Reader-in-Waiting; Hui firmly declined, and Teng Fu spoke to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hui also resigned remonstrance office when shifted to Reader-in-Waiting; he firmly declined, and Teng Fu appealed to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝詔甫曰：「繪抗跡孤遠，立朝寡援，不畏強禦，知無不為。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Fu: "Hui stands alone and distant, has few allies in court, fears no strong opposition, and knowing something does it without fail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Fu, "Hui stands alone in court, fearless before power, and acts on every conviction.

sentences.zh: 朕一見許其忠藎，擢置言職，信之亦篤矣。

translations.literal: At one meeting I approved his loyalty and forthrightness, elevated him to remonstrance office, and trusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: I recognized his loyalty at once, elevated him to remonstrance, and trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 今日之除，蓋難與宰相並立於輕重之間，姑令少避爾，卿其諭朕意。」

translations.literal: Today's appointment is because it is hard to stand with the chancellor between light and heavy—let him withdraw a little for now; you should convey My intent."
translations.idiomatic: This appointment is hard to reconcile with standing beside the chancellor in equal weight—let him step aside for now. Convey my intent."

sentences.zh: 繪曰：「諫官不得其言則去，經筵非姑息之地。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "If a remonstrance official cannot obtain his words he leaves—the classic lecture hall is no place for indulgence."
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "A remonstrator who cannot speak freely must leave—the lecture hall is no place for soft compromise."

sentences.zh: 卒不拜。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 未閱月，復知諫院，擢翰林學士，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed he again directed the Remonstrance Bureau, was elevated to Hanlin Academician, and made Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he again directed the Remonstrance Bureau, became Hanlin Academician, and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時安石用事，賢士多謝去。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Anshi held power and many worthy men resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi then held power, and many worthy men were leaving office.

sentences.zh: 繪言：「老成之人，不可不惜。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Men of long experience cannot but be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Hui warned, "The court cannot afford to lose its elder statesmen.

sentences.zh: 當今舊臣多引疾求去：范鎮年六十有三、呂誨五十有八、歐陽修六十有五而致仕；

translations.literal: Now many old ministers cite illness and seek to leave: Fan Zhen is sixty-three, Lü Hui fifty-eight, Ouyang Xiu sixty-five and retired;
translations.idiomatic: Already many veterans are retiring on illness: Fan Zhen at sixty-three, Lü Hui at fifty-eight, Ouyang Xiu at sixty-five;

sentences.zh: 富弼六十有八而引疾；

translations.literal: Fu Bi is sixty-eight and cites illness;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi at sixty-eight pleads illness;

sentences.zh: 司馬光、王陶皆五十而求散地，陛下可不思其故乎？」

translations.literal: Sima Guang and Wang Tao are both fifty and seek scattered posts—can Your Majesty not think on the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang and Wang Tao, both fifty, seek posts away from court—does Your Majesty not ask why?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「方今以經術取士，獨不用《春秋》，宜令學者以《三傳》解經。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Now scholars are taken by classical learning, yet the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 alone is not used—it should be ordered that scholars expound the classics through the 《Three Commentaries》."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that since examinations tested classical learning, the court should require scholars to expound the canon through the 《Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals》, not ignore the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 itself.

sentences.zh: 免役法行，繪陳十害。

translations.literal: When the Exemption-from-Corvée Law was implemented, Hui set forth ten harms.
translations.idiomatic: When the Exemption-from-Corvée Law took effect, Hui listed ten harms.

sentences.zh: 安石使曾布疏其說，詔繪分析，固執前議，遂罷為侍讀學士、知亳州，歷應天府、杭州。

translations.literal: Anshi had Zeng Bu refute his views; an edict ordered Hui to analyze them; he firmly held to his earlier opinion and was therefore dismissed to Reader-in-Waiting and prefect of Bo Prefecture, then successively Yingtian Prefecture and Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had Zeng Bu rebut him; ordered to respond, Hui held firm and was dismissed to Reader-in-Waiting and prefect of Bo, then Yingtian and Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 再為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He again became Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 議者欲加孔子帝號，繪以為非禮，又言不宜用遼曆改置閏，悉從之。
