translations.literal: Discussants wished to add an imperial title to Confucius; Hui thought this unorthodox, and also said the Liao calendar should not be used to reset intercalary months—all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed an imperial title for Confucius, Hui called it improper; he also opposed resetting intercalation by the Liao calendar—both views prevailed.

sentences.zh: 繪常薦屬吏王永年，御史蔡承禧言其私通饋賂，坐貶荊南節度副使。

translations.literal: Hui had often recommended his subordinate Wang Yongnian; Censor Cai Chenxi said he privately exchanged bribes, and Hui was demoted to military vice commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had recommended subordinate Wang Yongnian; Censor Cai Chenxi accused him of taking bribes through the appointment, and Hui was demoted to vice commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 詳在《竇卞傳》。

translations.literal: Details are in the 《Biography of Dou Bian》.
translations.idiomatic: For particulars see the 《Biography of Dou Bian》.

sentences.zh: 數月，分司南京，改提舉太平觀，起知興國軍。

translations.literal: After several months he served Nanjing in a divisional post, was changed to superintend the Taiping Abbey, and was raised to govern the Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he served Nanjing in a divisional post, superintended the Taiping Abbey, then governed the Xingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，復天章閣待制，再知杭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was restored as Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and again governed Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanyou he was restored as Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and again governed Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 繪為吏敏強，主愛利，而受性疏曠，訖以是見廢斥。

translations.literal: Hui as an official was sharp and strong, chiefly loving benefit, yet by nature he was broad and unconstrained—ultimately for this he was dismissed and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: As an official Hui was sharp and public-spirited, yet by nature broad and unconstrained—and for that he was eventually cast aside.

sentences.zh: 然表裏洞達，一出於誠，為范祖禹所諮重。

translations.literal: Yet inside and outside he was penetrating, all arising from sincerity, and Fan Zuyou consulted and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet transparent in motive and utterly sincere, he was deeply valued by Fan Zuyou.

sentences.zh: 為文立就，有集八十卷。

translations.literal: In writing he completed work at once; he had a collection of eighty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote with effortless speed and left a collection of eighty juan.

sentences.zh: 劉庠，字希道，彭城人。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang, styled Xidao, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang, courtesy name Xidao, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 八歲能詩。

translations.literal: At eight sui he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 蔡齊妻以子，用齊遺奏，補將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Cai Qi took him as son-in-law; using Qi's final memorial, he was appointed chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qi took him as son-in-law; through Qi's final memorial he entered service as chief clerk of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 復中進士第，為高密廣平院教授。

translations.literal: He again passed the jinshi examination and became professor at the Guangping Academy in Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: He later passed the jinshi examination and taught at the Guangping Academy in Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 英宗求直言，庠上書論時事。

translations.literal: When Yingzong sought blunt speech, Xiang submitted a memorial discussing current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong sought frank counsel, Liu Xiang submitted a memorial on current affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝以示韓琦，琦對之未識，帝益嘉重，除監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: The emperor showed it to Han Qi; Qi replied without recognizing him; the emperor prized him all the more and appointed him Acting Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed it to Han Qi, who did not know him; the emperor prized him all the more and made him Acting Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 日食甫數日，苑中張具待幸，庠言非所以祗天戒，詔罷之。

translations.literal: An eclipse had occurred only days before; in the park a feast was spread awaiting the imperial visit; Xiang said this was not how to revere Heaven's warning, and an edict canceled it.
translations.idiomatic: Days after an eclipse the palace park was prepared for a feast; Liu Xiang said this failed to honor Heaven's warning, and the feast was canceled.

sentences.zh: 會聖宮修仁宗神御殿，甚宏麗。

translations.literal: The Palace of Meeting with the Sage was repairing the spirit hall of Renzong—it was very grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace of Meeting with the Sage was building a magnificent spirit hall for Renzong.

sentences.zh: 庠言：「天子之孝，在繼先志，隆大業，不在宗廟之靡。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies in continuing the former will and enlarging the great enterprise—not in the extravagance of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang argued, "Imperial filial piety lies in carrying forward the former will and great enterprise—not in lavish ancestral halls.

sentences.zh: 宜損其制，以昭先帝儉德。」

translations.literal: The scale should be reduced to display the former emperor's frugal virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the scale to display the late emperor's frugality."

sentences.zh: 奉宸庫被盜，治守藏吏。

translations.literal: The Inner Treasury was robbed; the keepers were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Inner Treasury was robbed, the keepers were punished.

sentences.zh: 庠言：「皇城幾察厲禁，實近侍主之，當並按。」

translations.literal: Xiang said: "The Imperial City is strictly patrolled and forbidden, yet in fact it is managed by close attendants—they should be investigated together."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said, "The Imperial City is tightly guarded, yet close attendants actually control it—they should be investigated too."

sentences.zh: 仁宗外家李珣犯銷金法，庠奏言，法行當自貴近始。

translations.literal: Renzong's consort kin Li Xun violated the gilding prohibition; Xiang memorialized that when law is enforced it should begin with the honored and near.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong's consort kin Li Xun violated the gilding prohibition, Liu Xiang argued that law must begin with the high and near.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，儲嗣未正，庠拜疏謂：「太子，天下本。

translations.literal: The emperor was unwell and the heir was not settled; Xiang bowed in memorial saying: "The crown prince is the root of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill and the succession unsettled, Liu Xiang memorialized, "The crown prince is the root of the realm.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝於初元即為無窮計。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han at the beginning of Chuyuan already planned for endless generations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han at the opening of Chuyuan already planned for endless generations.

sentences.zh: 潁王長且賢，宜亟立，使日侍禁中，閱四方章奏。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Ying is eldest and worthy—he should quickly be established, daily attending within the forbidden palace and reviewing memorials from the four directions."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ying is eldest and worthy—establish him at once, let him daily attend within the palace and review memorials from every quarter."

sentences.zh: 帝皆行之。

translations.literal: The emperor carried out all these measures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted every proposal.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，遷殿中侍御史，為右司諫。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Xiang was transferred to Palace Censor-in-Attendance and made Right Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Liu Xiang became Palace Censor-in-Attendance and Right Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 言：「中國禦戎之策，守信為上。

translations.literal: He said: "China's policy for guarding against barbarians—keeping faith is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: He argued, "China's frontier policy should put keeping faith above all else.

sentences.zh: 昔元昊之叛，五來五得志，海內為之困弊。

translations.literal: Formerly when Yuanhao rebelled, five campaigns came and five times he got his will—the realm was exhausted and impoverished thereby.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, five campaigns brought five humiliations and exhausted the realm.

sentences.zh: 今莫若示大信、舍近功，為國家長利。」

translations.literal: Now it is best to display great faith, abandon near-term achievement, and seek the state's long benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Better to show great faith, abandon short-term gains, and seek the state's lasting good."

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹。

translations.literal: He was sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 故事，兩國忌日不相避。

translations.literal: By precedent the two states did not avoid one another's mourning days.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the two states did not observe one another's mourning days.

sentences.zh: 契丹張宴白溝，日當英宗祥祭，庠丐免，契丹義而聽之。

translations.literal: The Khitan spread a banquet at Bai Gou on the day of Yingzong's mourning sacrifice; Xiang begged exemption, and the Khitan, deeming it righteous, consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan held a banquet at Bai Gou on Yingzong's mourning day; Liu Xiang begged exemption, and they honorably consented.

sentences.zh: 除集賢殿修撰、河東轉運使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature and Transport Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He became Compiler of the Hall for Treasuring Literature and Transport Commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 庠計一路之產，鐵利為饒，請復舊冶鼓鑄，通隰州鹽礬，博易以濟用。

translations.literal: Xiang calculated the circuit's products—iron profits were abundant; he requested restoration of old smelting and casting, opening salt and alum of Xi Prefecture, and barter to meet needs.
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the circuit's resources, Liu Xiang found iron most profitable and proposed restoring old smelters, opening Xi Prefecture salt and alum, and trading to meet needs.

sentences.zh: 又請募民入粟塞下，豫為足食。

translations.literal: He also requested recruiting people to bring grain below the passes, preparing in advance for full provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed recruiting grain shipments to the frontier in advance of need.

sentences.zh: 進天章閣待制、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: He advanced to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and Transport Commissioner of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Court Gentleman of the Heavenly Manifest Hall and Transport Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 契丹侵霸州土場，或言河北不可不備。

translations.literal: The Khitan encroached on Ba Prefecture's soil fields; some said Hebei could not but be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan encroached on Ba Prefecture pasturelands, some urged full Hebei mobilization.

sentences.zh: 庠上五策，料其必不動，已而果然。

translations.literal: Xiang submitted five stratagems, calculating that they would certainly not move—and afterward it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang submitted five stratagems predicting they would not act—and so it proved.

sentences.zh: 大河東流，議者欲徙而北。

translations.literal: The great river flowed east; discussants wished to shift it north.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yellow River flowed east, some proposed diverting it north.

sentences.zh: 內侍程昉希功，請益兵濟役。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Cheng Fang hoped for merit and requested increased troops to aid the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Cheng Fang, seeking glory, asked for more troops to aid the work.

sentences.zh: 庠請遲以歲月，徐觀其勢而順導之。

translations.literal: Xiang requested delay over months, slowly observing its force and guiding it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang urged delay over months, watching the river's course and guiding it gradually.

sentences.zh: 朝廷是其議。

translations.literal: The court approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 移知真定府，又為河東都轉運使，召知開封府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Zhending Prefecture, again became Transport Commissioner of Hedong, and was summoned to govern Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Zhending Prefecture, again headed Hedong transport, and was summoned to govern Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 庠不肯屈事王安石。

translations.literal: Xiang would not bend to serve Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang would not bend to serve Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石欲見之，戒典謁者曰：「今日客至勿納，惟劉尹來，即告我。」

translations.literal: Anshi wished to see him and instructed the reception officer: "If guests come today do not admit them—only if Prefect Liu comes, then inform me."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi wished to see him and told the gatekeeper, "Admit no guests today—except Prefect Liu; inform me at once."

sentences.zh: 有語庠者曰：「王公意如此，盍一往見。」

translations.literal: Someone told Xiang: "Lord Wang's intent is thus—why not go once to see him?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Liu Xiang, "Lord Wang wants you—why not call on him once?"

sentences.zh: 庠謂：「見之，何所言？

translations.literal: Xiang said: "If I see him, what would I say?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang replied, "If I go, what would I say?

sentences.zh: 自彼執政，未嘗一事合人情。

translations.literal: Since he took power, not one matter has accorded with human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Since he took power, not one policy has accorded with human feeling.

sentences.zh: 脫問青苗、免役，將何辭以對？」

translations.literal: If he asks about the Green Sprouts or Exemption-from-Corvée laws, with what words shall I reply?"
translations.idiomatic: If he asks about Green Sprouts or Exemption-from-Corvée, what answer could I give?"

sentences.zh: 竟不往。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He never went.

sentences.zh: 奏論新法，神宗諭之曰：「奈何不與大臣協心濟治乎？」

translations.literal: Memorializing on the new laws, Shenzong instructed him: "Why not join the great ministers in coordinated effort to govern?"
translations.idiomatic: Memorializing against the new laws, Liu Xiang was told by Shenzong, "Why not join the great ministers in common effort?"

sentences.zh: 庠曰：「臣子於君父各伸其志。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Ministers and sons each extend their will to sovereign and father.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang answered, "Ministers and sons each serve sovereign and father according to their own conscience.

sentences.zh: 臣知事陛下，不敢附安石。」

translations.literal: Your servant knows how to serve Your Majesty and dares not attach himself to Anshi."
translations.idiomatic: I know how to serve Your Majesty—I dare not attach myself to Anshi."

sentences.zh: 會與蔡確爭廷參禮，遂以為龍圖閣直學士、知太原府。

translations.literal: When he contended with Cai Que over court-audience ritual, he was therefore made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After quarreling with Cai Que over court-audience ritual, he was posted as Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 請復憲州募民子弟剽銳工技擊者，籍為勇敢，仿漢謫戍法，貰流以下罪徙實河外。

translations.literal: He requested restoring Xian Prefecture, recruiting youths who were sharp, skilled in crafts and fighting, registering them as the Brave, imitating Han's exiled frontier garrison law, commuting exile and lesser punishments to populate lands beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed restoring Xian Prefecture, enrolling sharp young craftsmen and fighters as "the Brave," and populating the far frontier by commuting exile and lesser sentences after the Han model.

sentences.zh: 契丹建牙雲中，遣騎涉內地，邊吏執之。

translations.literal: The Khitan established headquarters at Yunzhong and sent horsemen crossing inner territory; border officials seized them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pitched headquarters at Yunzhong and sent horsemen across the border; frontier officials seized them.

sentences.zh: 契丹檄取紛然，又遣使議疆事。

translations.literal: Khitan dispatches demanding their return came in confusion, and they also sent envoys to discuss border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan demands for their return poured in, and envoys came to discuss the border.

sentences.zh: 眾疑其造兵端，欲大為備。

translations.literal: The multitude suspected they were creating a military pretext and wished to make great preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Many suspected war and urged massive preparations.

sentences.zh: 庠奏言：「雲朔歲儉，軍無見糧。

translations.literal: Xiang memorialized: "Yun and Shuo have lean years; the armies have no ready grain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang memorialized, "Yun and Shuo face famine; Khitan armies lack ready grain.

sentences.zh: 契丹張形示強，造端首禍，曲在彼不在我，願勿聽。

translations.literal: The Khitan display strength to show form; they create the pretext and begin the trouble—the wrong is on their side, not ours—I beg you not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: They show force but begin the trouble—the fault is theirs, not ours. Do not heed them.

sentences.zh: 宜先諭以理，然後飭兵觀釁。」

translations.literal: First instruct them with reason, then order troops and watch for provocation."
translations.idiomatic: Reason with them first, then ready troops and watch for provocation."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉使者辭順，訖以黃嵬山分水嶺立新疆。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the envoy's compliant words; in the end a new border was set at the watershed of Mount Huangwei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the envoy's conciliatory words; in the end a new border was fixed at Mount Huangwei watershed.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，服終，知成都府。

translations.literal: He suffered his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he governed Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he governed Chengdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乞禁西山六州與漢人婚姻，勿蹈吐蕃取維州之害。

translations.literal: He requested forbidding marriage between the six western mountain prefectures and Han people, lest they repeat the harm of Tibet's taking Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to forbid marriage between the six western mountain prefectures and Han people, lest history repeat Tibet's seizure of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His next posting was Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐失舉，降知虢州，移江寧府、滁州，徙永興軍。

translations.literal: For failure in recommendation he was demoted to prefect of Guo Prefecture, moved to Jiangning and Chu Prefectures, and transferred to the Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: For a failed recommendation he was demoted to Guo Prefecture, then moved through Jiangning and Chu Prefectures to the Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 時西征無功，關內騷動。

translations.literal: At the time the western campaign had no success and the passes were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The failed western campaign had thrown the passes into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 庠過關，力言虛內事外，恐搖根本，帝感納其忠。

translations.literal: Xiang, passing the frontier, forcefully spoke of emptying the interior to serve the exterior and feared shaking the root; the emperor was moved and accepted his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the frontier, Liu Xiang warned that draining the interior to serve foreign campaigns would shake the realm's foundations; the emperor was moved and heeded him.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，加樞密直學士、知渭州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was given Direct Academician of the Privy Council and made prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanyou he became Direct Academician of the Privy Council and prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 宣仁聞之曰：「帥臣極難得，劉庠可惜也。」

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren, on hearing it, said: "A frontier commander is extremely hard to obtain—Liu Xiang is to be regretted."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren said on hearing of it, "A frontier commander is hard to find—Liu Xiang is a loss."

sentences.zh: 庠有吏能，淹通歷代史，王安石稱其博。

translations.literal: Xiang had administrative ability, was thoroughly versed in successive dynastic histories, and Wang Anshi praised his breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang was an able administrator, deeply versed in successive dynasties' histories; even Wang Anshi praised his erudition.

sentences.zh: 卒後，蘇頌論庠治平建儲之功，詔褒錄其子。

translations.literal: After his death Su Song discussed Xiang's merit in establishing the heir during the Zhiping era, and an edict praised and enfeoffed his sons.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Su Song memorialized Liu Xiang's merit in securing the succession during Zhiping, and the court enfeoffed his sons.

sentences.zh: 朱京，字世昌，南豐人。

translations.literal: Zhu Jing, styled Shichang, was a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jing, courtesy name Shichang, came from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 父軾，有隱德。

translations.literal: His father Shi had hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi was a man of quiet virtue.

sentences.zh: 京博學淹貫，登進士甲科。

translations.literal: Jing was broadly learned and thoroughly versed, and passed the jinshi examination in the top class.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and deeply versed, Jing passed the jinshi examination in the top class.

sentences.zh: 教授亳州、應天府，入為太學錄。

translations.literal: He lectured at Bo and Yingtian Prefectures and entered court as Recorder of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He taught at Bo and Yingtian Prefectures, then entered court as Recorder of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 神宗數召見論事，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong repeatedly summoned him to discuss affairs and elevated him to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong repeatedly summoned him to discuss affairs and made him Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時中丞及同僚多罷去，京抗疏曰：「御史假之則重，略之則輕。

translations.literal: At the time the vice censor-in-chief and colleagues were mostly dismissed; Jing submitted a bold memorial saying: "Censors are heavy if relied upon, light if neglected.
translations.idiomatic: As the vice censor-in-chief and many colleagues were dismissed, Jing submitted a bold memorial: "Censors matter when heeded and mean nothing when brushed aside.

sentences.zh: 今耳目之官，屢進屢卻，則言者不若靜默為賢，直者不若柔從為智。

translations.literal: Now the eyes and ears of the court are repeatedly promoted and repeatedly removed—then speakers are not as good as the silent, and the upright not as wise as the soft and compliant.
translations.idiomatic: When the court's eyes and ears are repeatedly installed and removed, silence looks wiser than speech and compliance smarter than integrity.

sentences.zh: 偷安取容，雖得此百數，亦何益國邪？」

translations.literal: Seeking ease and acceptance—even if one obtains a hundred such men, what benefit to the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Men who seek ease and favor—even a hundred of them—what good are they to the state?"

sentences.zh: 他日入見，帝勞之曰：「昨覽奏疏，所補多矣。」

translations.literal: Another day entering audience, the emperor comforted him: "Yesterday I read your memorial—it added much."
translations.idiomatic: On a later audience the emperor said warmly, "I read your memorial yesterday—it added much."

sentences.zh: 京風神峻整，見者憚之，目為真御史。

translations.literal: Jing's bearing was stern and ordered; those who saw him feared him, and he was called a true censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's bearing was stern and imposing; men feared him and called him a true censor.

sentences.zh: 初，臺臣奏事，必先移閤門，得班乃入。

translations.literal: At first, when censors reported affairs they had first to notify the Gate of Transmission and only after receiving a court session could they enter.
translations.idiomatic: Originally censors had to notify the Gate of Transmission and wait for a court session before entering.

sentences.zh: 京嘗以名聞，翌旦既入，會有先之者，不及對而退。

translations.literal: Jing once had his name announced; the next morning he had entered when someone preceded him—he could not respond and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jing once had his name entered; next morning he arrived but another spoke first and he withdrew without being heard.

sentences.zh: 帝問京安在，左右以告，詔趣之入，辰漏且盡，為留班以須。

translations.literal: The emperor asked where Jing was; attendants told him; an edict hurried him in—the morning clock was nearly exhausted, and the emperor kept the session to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked where Jing was; told, he ordered him hurried in—the morning audience was nearly over, yet the emperor held session to wait.

sentences.zh: 未幾，論大臣除擬有愛憎之私。

translations.literal: Before long he discussed chief ministers' appointments and removals having partiality of love and hate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he criticized chief ministers for favoritism in appointments.

sentences.zh: 中書言其失實，謫監興國軍鹽稅。

translations.literal: The Secretariat said his charges were untrue and demoted him to supervise salt tax at the Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat declared his charges false and demoted him to supervise salt tax at the Xingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 歷太常博士、湖北、京西、江東轉運判官，提點淮西刑獄、司封員外郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, transport assesor of Hubei, Jingxi, and Jiangdong, intendant of Huaixi judicial affairs, and Outer Section Member of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, transport assessor on Hubei, Jingxi, and Jiangdong circuits, Huaixi judicial intendant, and Outer Section Member of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元符初，遷國子司業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfu he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanfu he became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 京在元祐時，嘗為《幸太學頌》，或擿其語有及先朝者，京亦固辭不拜。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou Jing had written 《Ode on the Imperial Visit to the Directorate of Education》; some picked out language touching on the former reign, and Jing also firmly declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou Jing had written 《Ode on the Imperial Visit to the Directorate of Education》; critics found language touching the former reign, and he firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初立，復命之，逾月而卒。

translations.literal: When Huizong first ascended the throne he was again appointed; after more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong first took the throne Jing was again appointed; he died within a month.

sentences.zh: 論曰：何郯、吳中復，皆良御史也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: He Tan and Wu Zhongfu were both good censors.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: He Tan and Wu Zhongfu were both worthy censors.

sentences.zh: 郯出夏竦，阻王守忠，奸人庶幾少戢矣。

translations.literal: Tan drove out Xia Song and blocked Wang Shouzhong—wicked men were perhaps somewhat restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Tan expelled Xia Song and blocked Wang Shouzhong, giving villains at least some pause.

sentences.zh: 中復恥識面臺官，其所守可見矣。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was ashamed of censors who knew their superiors by sight—his integrity can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu scorned censors chosen by acquaintance—his integrity speaks for itself.

sentences.zh: 薦之論李定，思恭之右歐陽修，繪請惜老成，庠不附新法，數子所見，何其同也。

translations.literal: Jian's discussion of Li Ding, Sigong's support of Ouyang Xiu, Hui's plea to cherish elder statesmen, and Xiang's refusal to attach to the new laws—how alike were these men's views!
translations.idiomatic: Jian on Li Ding, Sigong defending Ouyang Xiu, Hui pleading to keep elder statesmen, Xiang refusing the new laws—how alike their vision was.

sentences.zh: 獵為令而興孔子廟，孟陽以教授而參決大計，此其卓然者乎。

translations.literal: Lie as magistrate raised a Confucian temple; Mengyang as instructor helped decide a great plan—these were their outstanding deeds, were they not?
translations.idiomatic: Lie built a Confucian temple as magistrate; Mengyang as instructor helped settle a great succession—were these not their finest moments?

sentences.zh: 恢臨政簡約，無可議者。

translations.literal: Hui's governance was simple and restrained—nothing to criticize.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Hui governed simply and without reproach.

sentences.zh: 京持論端確，竟以去位，君子惜之。

translations.literal: Jing held his views upright and exact, yet in the end lost his post—men of worth regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing argued with upright precision, yet lost office in the end—a loss men of principle regretted.
